newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Occidental says it hopes to seal Bangladesh fire.
newsitem.headline: Occidental says it hopes to seal Bangladesh fire.

text.p: U.S. Occidental Petroleum Corp is planning to drill a relief well to tame a gas well which has been blazing for more than a month, state-owned Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petrobangla) said in a statement on Monday.
The fire follows an explosion that damaged forest and tea plantations in Bangladesh's northeastern Magurchhara area.
The statement said Occidental hoped to start work on the relief well by the middle of August.
Nigel Hopkinson, Bangladesh chief of Occidental, told Reuters his company would drill a relief well with a new rig near the burning well to seal off gas at the bottom.
The gas well at Magurchhara in northeastern Maulvi Bazar district was still burning on Monday after it exploded on June 15 when a rig hit a shallow "trap gas" layer.
Petrobangla said on Monday the pressure of gas was not likely to cause another explosion.
Petrobangla officials said Gary Burtchaell, vice-president of Occidental, had talks recently with Bangladesh energy ministry officials on how his company could stop the fire.
The talks also covered rehabilitation of dozens of tribal families displaced by the fire and compensation for losses to tea plantations.
Bangladesh said the fire drove away Khasia tribal families and wild animals from their natural habitat in about two km (1.2 miles) of hill-top forests.
Occidental, which owns rights to explore for hydrocarbons in the entire northeastern Sylhet region, plans to spend $100 million on exploring the area.
Petrobangla officials said Occidental was also likely to provide assistance for speedy installation of alternative rail tracks damaged by the gas field fire.
"We are closely working with various government departments...some of them involve compensation. We have agreed to provide compensation to displaced families," Hopkinson said.
